proofs.proof_tex:
Assume \(\operatorname{rank}(M)<K\).  Then there is \(0\ne a\in\ker(M)\).  Fix positive intensities \(\lambda_{rd}\) and \(0\ne u\in[0,\infty)^p\), and choose the nonzero \(\epsilon\) required by \(\mathrm{def{:}positive\text{-}poisson\text{-}alias}\).  For every \(r,d\),
\[
\lambda_{rd}(\epsilon)
\geq\lambda_{rd}-|\epsilon a_ru_d|
>\frac{\lambda_{rd}}2>0. \tag{7}
\]
Thus the baseline and perturbed type laws are both products of positive Poisson masses and have full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\).  Since \(a\ne0\) and \(u\ne0\), some product \(a_ru_d\) is nonzero, so those two labeled collections are distinct.

Under exact additive pooling and cell independence, the pooled coordinate \(d\) in row \(j\) is Poisson with intensity
\[
\sum_{r=1}^KM_{jr}\lambda_{rd}(\epsilon)
=\sum_{r=1}^KM_{jr}\lambda_{rd}
+\epsilon (Ma)_ju_d
=\sum_{r=1}^KM_{jr}\lambda_{rd}. \tag{8}
\]
All pooled coordinates are independent in both constructions.  Equation (8) therefore makes their entire row-wise pooled laws identical.  Independent replication and type invariance place both constructions in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), completing the witness.

For \(z\in(0,1]^p\), \(z^V>0\) almost surely, so \(G_r(z)>0\).  Exact additive pooling, mutual cell independence, and type invariance give
\[
H_j(z)
=\mathbb E\!\left[
z^{\sum_{r,c}V_{jirc}}\right]
=\prod_{r=1}^KG_r(z)^{M_{jr}}. \tag{9}
\]
Consequently, with coordinatewise real logarithms,
\[
\log H(z)=M\log G(z). \tag{10}
\]
This is the count-PGF instance of the log-transform linearization credited to the cited Shih--Hero transform precedent.

If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\), the Moore--Penrose inverse satisfies
\[
M^+M=(M^{\mathsf T}M)^{-1}M^{\mathsf T}M=I_K.
\]
Multiplying (10) and exponentiating coordinatewise proves
\[
G(z)=\exp\{M^+\log H(z)\}=\mathscr R_M(H)(z). \tag{11}
\]
Thus equality of pooled-law tuples implies equality of every component PGF on \((0,1)^p\).  To see directly that this identifies the law, subtract two component PGFs.  Fix \(p-1\) coordinates in \((0,1)\), view the difference as an absolutely convergent one-variable power series, and apply the continuation-and-least-nonzero-coefficient argument proved in the regularity lemma.  Its coefficients, which are power series in the remaining coordinates, vanish; repeating coordinate by coordinate shows that every coefficient vanishes.  Since the coefficient of \(z^v\) is \(P_r(\{v\})\), the component laws coincide.  Hence \(\mathscr A_M\) is injective.

Conversely, when \(\operatorname{rank}(M)<K\), the proved positive-Poisson alias lemma gives two distinct labeled full-support component-law tuples in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\) having identical pooled laws.  Therefore \(\mathscr A_M\) is not injective.  This establishes both directions and the explicit recovery map.

Fix a member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\) and one type \(r\).  In a topological ordering, every root Poisson mass is strictly positive, and every non-root conditional Poisson mass is strictly positive because its rate is an intercept plus nonnegative terms with a strictly positive intercept.  Therefore
\[
\Pr_\theta(V=v)=\prod_{s=1}^p
p_{rs,\theta}(v_s\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{d_r}(s)})>0
\quad\text{for every }v\in\mathbb N_0^p. \tag{12}
\]
This proves full support.

Let \(U_{rs}\), over all nodes and types, be mutually independent
\(\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) variables.  Generate each root and then each non-root in topological order by the generalized inverse of its stipulated Poisson conditional distribution evaluated at \(U_{rs}\).  This realizes exactly (12), and the exogenous variables are jointly independent.  Hence causal sufficiency holds.

It remains to verify the stated pairwise condition.  Fix an edge \(k\to s\) and any admissible conditioning set \(S\) with
\[
\operatorname{pa}(s)\setminus\{k\}\subseteq S
\subseteq\operatorname{nd}(s)\setminus\{k,s\}.
\]
By (12), the event \(V_S=0\) has positive probability, and conditional on this event the retained cause \(V_k\) has support \(\mathbb N_0\).  With all other parents fixed at zero, the effect rate is
\[
\lambda_s(x)=\alpha_s+b_{sk}x^{q_{sk}},
\qquad \alpha_s>0,\quad b_{sk}>0,\quad q_{sk}\in\mathbb N. \tag{13}
\]
The DAG factorization gives the local Markov property, so conditioning additionally on nondescendants in \(S\) that are not parents does not change this conditional kernel once all parents are fixed.
It is strictly increasing and unbounded.  The cited Poisson-CPCM reversibility result says that a nonidentifiable bivariate Poisson direction must instead have rate \(\exp(ax+b)\) with \(a<0\), which is strictly decreasing.  Thus (13) cannot be exceptional.  Every required conditioned pair is identifiable; when there are no edges the requirement is vacuous.  The three defining conditions of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\) now hold, proving inclusion.

Under the fixed protocol and an intervention \(V_1=x\), the second node has
\[
V_2\mid\operatorname{do}(V_1=x)\sim
\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda_x),\qquad \lambda_x=1+x^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
\mathbb E[V_2\mid\operatorname{do}(V_1=x)]=\lambda_x.
\]
The third conditional mean is \(1+x+V_2^2\).  Since a Poisson variable of mean \(\lambda\) has second moment \(\lambda+\lambda^2\), iterated expectation gives
\[
\mathbb E[V_3\mid\operatorname{do}(V_1=x)]
=1+x+\lambda_x+\lambda_x^2. \tag{14}
\]
At \(x=1\), the two displayed means are \(2\) and \(8\); at \(x=2\), they are \(5\) and \(33\).  Subtracting the \(x=1\) values from the \(x=2\) values gives
\[
\tau_{i_Y,r}=5-2=3,\qquad
\tau_{i_Z,r}=33-8=25.
\]
The conditional kernels other than that of the intervened coordinate are exactly those retained by the declared truncated factorization, so these are the causal contrasts in the proposition for each type.

Full column rank and the rank-frontier theorem first identify each labeled component law \(P_r\) from the pooled-law tuple.  This is an equality between the causal model's observational law and the observable recovery functional, not a definition of a causal effect.

For a recovered \(P_r\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\), causal sufficiency and pairwise identifiability are part of the class definition.  The cited CPCM DAG-identification lemma therefore implies that its labeled generating graph \(D_r\) is the unique CPCM DAG compatible with \(P_r\).  Applying this separately to the labeled columns of \(M\) identifies the entire graph tuple.

Now suppose the recovered model lies in
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\).  By polynomial-class inclusion it has full support.  Hence, for every parent configuration,
\[
p_{rs}(v_s\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)})
=\frac{\Pr_{P_r}(V_s=v_s,\,
V_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}=v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)})}
{\Pr_{P_r}(V_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)}
=v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)})} \tag{15}
\]
is an identified ratio with a strictly positive denominator.  Independent exogenous variables give modular structural assignments.  Replacing the equation for \(V_{i_X}\) by the constant \(x\) therefore deletes precisely its observational factor, while the remaining kernels are unchanged.  Successive summation in a topological order proves that
\[
P_r^{\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=x)}(v_{-i_X})
=\prod_{s\ne i_X}
p_{rs}(v_s\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_{D_r}(s)})
\big|_{v_{i_X}=x} \tag{16}
\]
is normalized.  This is the standard truncated-factorization consequence of the structural model, and proves its equality to the causal intervention law rather than stipulating that equality as the estimand.

Finally, Poisson conditional moments are polynomials in their rates.  Induction in topological order, with the positive-polynomial rates, shows that all polynomial moments in (16) are finite for the fixed interventions \(x=1,2\).  Thus the two expectations in each contrast exist.  Equations (15)--(16), followed by the two indicated summations and subtraction, are an observable functional of the recovered law and graph and equal the causal target.  Hence the pooled-law tuple identifies \(\boldsymbol\tau\).

Fix \(z\in\mathcal Z_\eta\).  Monotonicity of \(z^v\) in every coordinate gives
\[
G_r(z)\geq G_r(\eta,\ldots,\eta)=\gamma_r.
\]
Equation (9) then gives \(H_j(z)\geq\prod_r\gamma_r^{M_{jr}}\geq\beta\).  Since every coordinate error is at most its Euclidean norm,
\[
\widetilde H_j(z)\geq H_j(z)-\delta\geq\beta-\delta>0. \tag{17}
\]
The scalar mean-value theorem for the logarithm and (17) imply
\[
|\log\widetilde H_j(z)-\log H_j(z)|
\leq\frac{|\widetilde H_j(z)-H_j(z)|}{\beta-\delta}.
\]
Taking Euclidean norms and using the definition of \(\delta\) yields
\[
\|\log\widetilde H(z)-\log H(z)\|_2
\leq\frac{\delta}{\beta-\delta}. \tag{18}
\]
Under full column rank, the rank-frontier identity is
\(M^+\log H(z)=\log G(z)\).  Submultiplicativity applied to (18) proves
\[
\|M^+\log\widetilde H(z)-\log G(z)\|_2
\leq \|M^+\|_2\frac{\delta}{\beta-\delta}=E_M. \tag{19}
\]

Write \(\Delta=M^+\log\widetilde H-\log G\).  Since \(0<G_r\leq1\),
\[
|\exp(\log G_r+\Delta_r)-G_r|
=G_r|e^{\Delta_r}-1|
\leq e^{|\Delta_r|}|\Delta_r|
\leq e^{E_M}|\Delta_r|.
\]
Summing squares proves the second asserted bound.  Division by \(G_r>0\) gives
\[
\left|\frac{\mathscr R_M(\widetilde H)_r}{G_r}-1\right|
=|e^{\Delta_r}-1|
\leq e^{|\Delta_r|}-1\leq e^{E_M}-1.
\]
All bounds are independent of \(z\); taking the stated suprema completes the proof.

Apply the polynomial-PGF regularity lemma to each of the finitely many graph tuples.  Write \(F_{\boldsymbol d}(\theta,z)\) for the stacked type PGFs at a single point \(z\in\mathcal O\).  If \(v\) is a unit parameter direction, injectivity of the distributional differential and signed-PGF uniqueness imply that
\[
D_\theta F_{\boldsymbol d}(\theta,z)v\ne0
\quad\text{for some }z\in\mathcal O. \tag{20}
\]
For fixed \(\boldsymbol d\), the product of \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\) and its parameter unit sphere is compact.  Continuity makes the nonvanishing in (20) persist on a neighborhood of \((\theta,v)\).  A finite subcover supplies finitely many points \(z\) such that their stacked Jacobian has trivial kernel for every \(\theta\).  Its smallest singular value is continuous, so its minimum on \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\) is positive.

Uniform continuity of this finite stacked Jacobian gives a number \(r_0>0\) for which the integral Taylor formula separates every within-graph pair at distance less than \(r_0\).  Fix a positive rational \(r_1<r_0\).  Within a graph, two distinct parameters induce different laws.  If their PGFs agreed on the nonempty open set \(\mathcal O\), successive one-variable power-series uniqueness would make their laws equal, a contradiction.  On the compact set
\[
\{(\theta,\theta')\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}^2:
\|\theta-\theta'\|_2\geq r_1\}, \tag{21}
\]
each pair is consequently separated by some PGF evaluation.  A finite subcover of (21) supplies finitely many separating points.  The same argument applies to each compact product
\(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\times\Theta_{\boldsymbol d'}\) for
\(\boldsymbol d\ne\boldsymbol d'\), because the regularity lemma gives disjoint law images.

Take the union of all points selected in the preceding two paragraphs.  There are only finitely many graph tuples and graph pairs.  All the asserted full-rank and separation properties are strict and uniform on compact sets.  Joint continuity in the evaluation points permits each selected point to be perturbed to a rational point still in the open set \(\mathcal O\), without losing any property.  Denote the resulting finite rational grid by \(\mathcal T\).  It gives
\[
\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0,\qquad
\Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0
\]
when a wrong graph exists; the declared \(+\infty\) convention handles a singleton graph class.

We next construct the local charts, because Jacobian rank alone does not prove global injectivity.  At every \(\theta\), full column rank of
\(J_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta)\) gives a real left inverse
\[
L_\theta=(J^{\mathsf T}J)^{-1}J^{\mathsf T},
\qquad L_\theta J=I.
\]
Approximate \(L_\theta\) closely enough by a rational matrix \(P_\theta\).  Continuity of \(J\) then supplies a relative neighborhood \(U_\theta\) in the box on which
\[
\frac{P_\theta J(\vartheta)+
J(\vartheta)^{\mathsf T}P_\theta^{\mathsf T}}2
\succeq c_\theta I,\qquad c_\theta>0. \tag{22}
\]
Compactness and the rational rectangular shape of the parameter box give a finite cover by closed rational sub-boxes \(C_{\boldsymbol d c}\), each lying in one such neighborhood and carrying its corresponding rational \(P_{\boldsymbol d c}\), whose relative interiors still cover the parameter box.  A Lebesgue number of this finite relative open cover is positive.  Choose rational \(r_{\mathrm{id}}>0\) smaller than that number and smaller than \(r_1\).  Then every pair less than \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) apart is co-contained in a chart.

For \(\theta,\theta'\) in one convex chart, put \(\Delta=\theta'-\theta\).  The fundamental theorem of calculus and (22) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\langle P_{\boldsymbol d c}\{m(\theta')-m(\theta)\},\Delta\rangle
&=\int_0^1
\Delta^{\mathsf T}P_{\boldsymbol d c}
J(\theta+t\Delta)\Delta\,dt\\
&=\int_0^1
\Delta^{\mathsf T}\frac{PJ+J^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}}2
\Delta\,dt\\
&\geq c_{\boldsymbol d c}\|\Delta\|_2^2 .
\end{aligned} \tag{23}
\]
The finite minimum of the positive chart constants proves
\(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0\).

Finally, the remote set with distance at least \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) is compact.  Pairs at distance at least \(r_1\) are separated by the finite-cover points selected from (21), while pairs at distance in \([r_{\mathrm{id}},r_1]\) are separated by the local Taylor bound from the uniformly nonsingular stacked Jacobian.  Hence the already selected finite grid separates the whole remote set, so its continuous squared \(W\)-distance has a positive minimum, namely
\(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})>0\); if the set is empty the declared value is \(+\infty\).  A local pair is separated by (23), and a remote pair by this last bound.  Thus every within-graph moment map is globally injective, with the four distinct margins claimed.

All loops in \(\mathfrak C\) range over finite graph sets, finite state truncations, finite multi-index tables, finite precision lists, and binary trees of fixed depth.  A binary tree of depth \(d\) has at most \(2^d\) leaves.  Product-box trees are bounded more coarsely by \(4^{b_{\max}}\).  Summing over graph charts, graph objectives, same-graph remote products, and unordered wrong-graph products gives at most
\[
G_{\#}2^{c_{\max}}+G_{\#}2^{b_{\max}}
+\left(G_{\#}+\binom{G_{\#}}2\right)4^{b_{\max}}. \tag{24}
\]
The precision loop has
\[
P_{\mathrm{ar}}=
1+\left\lceil\frac{b_{\mathrm{cap}}-b_0}{\Delta b}\right\rceil
\]
passes.  By the literal operation accounting in
\(\mathrm{def{:}arithmetic\text{-}complexity}\), each pass and leaf uses at most the displayed recurrence cost plus the displayed cubic linear-algebra cost.  Multiplication by the leaf ceiling, including its extra terminal task, is exactly \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\).  This proves termination and both ceilings.

We prove enclosure soundness by induction through the procedure.  For a conditional Poisson variable,
\[
\mathbb E[V_s^m\mid V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)}]
=\sum_{k=0}^m
\left\{\begin{matrix}m\\k\end{matrix}\right\}\lambda_s^k.
\]
For \(h_s=1+|\operatorname{pa}(s)|\), convexity gives
\[
\left(\alpha_s+\sum_u b_{su}V_u^{q_{su}}\right)^k
\leq h_s^{k-1}\left(\alpha_s^k+
\sum_u b_{su}^kV_u^{q_{su}k}\right). \tag{25}
\]
Topological induction proves that every \(U_{\boldsymbol d rs}(m)\) majorizes its corresponding raw moment.  The same proof holds after the intervention deletes one kernel and substitutes a fixed count.

For a multi-index \(\nu\), direct differentiation of a Poisson log mass and the uniform lower rate \(\lambda^-_{rs}>0\) bounds its first derivative by \(L_{e_t}\) and its higher derivatives by \(L_\nu\).  The multivariate Leibniz rule then shows inductively that
\[
|\partial^\nu p_\theta(v)|\leq p_\theta(v)D_\nu(v). \tag{26}
\]
If \(T_R=\{v:\text{some }v_s>R_s\}\), the union bound and
\(\mathbf1\{v_s>R_s\}\leq v_s^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}/(R_s+1)^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}\)
give from (26)
\[
\sum_{v\in T_R}|\partial^\nu p_\theta(v)|
\leq\sum_s
\frac{\mathcal U_{\boldsymbol d r}(D_\nu V_s^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}})}
{(R_s+1)^{s_{\mathrm{tail}}}}
=E_{\boldsymbol d r,\nu}. \tag{27}
\]
Multiplication by \(V_{i_Y}+V_{i_Z}\) proves the intervention-contrast version.  The inequality
\[
|ab-\widetilde a\widetilde b|
\leq |a||b-\widetilde b|
+|\widetilde b||a-\widetilde a|
\leq2\varepsilon_0+\varepsilon_0^2
\]
when \(a,b\in[0,1]\) and both errors are at most \(\varepsilon_0\), proves the covariance-product enlargement.

For \(x\geq0\), Taylor's theorem at zero gives
\[
\left|e^{-x}-\sum_{k=0}^{a}\frac{(-x)^k}{k!}\right|
\leq\frac{x^{a+1}}{(a+1)!}, \tag{28}
\]
so the initial exponential interval is valid.  The Poisson recurrence, the complete-Bell recurrence, the multivariate Leibniz recurrence, and the fixed Taylor formula preserve enclosure by induction.  Equation (27) then enlarges retained sums to enclose the exact infinite sums.  Finally, downward rounding of lower endpoints and upward rounding of upper endpoints preserve every exact value under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division whenever the divisor interval excludes zero.  Thus every interval recorded by the procedure contains its exact untruncated target.

A positive lower endpoint for a wrong-graph or remote objective is therefore a valid lower bound for every point in that leaf.  The coverage checks make the passing leaves cover the entire required feasible set, proving
\[
\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T},\quad
\Lambda_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}.
\]
The interval \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) tests certify positive definiteness of
\(J^{\mathsf T}J-u^2I\) and of
\((PJ+J^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T})/2-uI\), proving respectively
\[
\kappa_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0,\qquad
\mu_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}>0. \tag{29}
\]
Exact rational endpoint comparisons similarly certify box validity, rank, simplex normalization, positive row masses, interior clearance, covariance denominators, variance upper bounds, and \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq N_{\max}\).  The simplex test is ordered before every covariance and well calculation, proving the stated early rejection.

For a Krawczyk collision test, every Jacobian is enclosed and the cited Krawczyk inclusion theorem gives a zero of the selected square moment difference inside the product box.  Singleton zero enclosures for all omitted coordinates make it a zero of the full moment difference.  Disjoint parameter factors then give a genuine wrong-graph collision.  Exact rank defect, invalid rational boxes, and simplex failure are themselves the other named obstructions.  Therefore every \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) status proves its recorded obstruction.  By definition no conclusion is attached to an exhausted or failed test, so \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\) is substantively silent.  Empty comparison sets are handled by their declared \(+\infty\) conventions.

Apply the stratified PGF limit separately to the independent training and inference splits.  It gives
\[
\widehat g_A\overset p\longrightarrow g_0,\qquad
\widehat g_B\overset p\longrightarrow g_0,\qquad
\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat g_B-g_0)
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_g). \tag{30}
\]
Certification gives full rank, positive normalized row fractions, positive wrong-graph separation, global within-graph identification, a positive Jacobian margin, and positive clearance of every inference box.  The polynomial regularity lemma gives continuity on every compact graph box and continuous differentiability near the truth.

For any graph \(\boldsymbol d\), the minimized criterion is continuous in its data argument.  More explicitly, because every moment vector lies in the compact cube and \(W\) is fixed,
\[
\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}}
\left|Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta;\widehat g_A)
-Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta;g_0)\right|
\leq C\|\widehat g_A-g_0\|_2
+\|W\|_2\|\widehat g_A-g_0\|_2^2=o_p(1) \tag{31}
\]
for a finite deterministic \(C\), uniformly over the finite graph set.  The true graph has population minimum zero.  Every wrong graph has population minimum at least
\(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0\).  Equation (31) and the fixed graph tie order therefore imply
\[
\Pr(\widehat{\boldsymbol D}=\boldsymbol D_0)\longrightarrow1. \tag{32}
\]

On the true graph, the certified global-identification lemma makes \(\theta_0\) the unique population minimum.  Compactness, (31) for the inference split, and the cited extremum-consistency theorem give
\(\widehat\theta\to_p\theta_0\) on the event in (32).  Positive inference-box clearance and the true-parameter interior assumption make the exact global minimizer interior with probability tending to one.  Put
\[
J_0=J_{\boldsymbol D_0,\mathcal T}(\theta_0).
\]
Certification gives \(\sigma_{\min}(J_0)>0\); with \(W\succ0\), \(J_0^{\mathsf T}WJ_0\) is invertible.  The cited minimum-distance theorem, with (30), yields
\[
\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)
=(J_0^{\mathsf T}WJ_0)^{-1}J_0^{\mathsf T}W
\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat g_B-g_0)+o_p(1), \tag{33}
\]
and the covariance in (33) is exactly
\(V_\theta(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0)\).

The training event in (32) is independent of the inference split.  For any bounded continuous test function, replacing the selected estimator by the true-graph estimator changes its expectation by at most twice the function bound times the probability of the complement of (32).  Thus the same limit holds unconditionally.  Differentiability of the fixed truncated-factorization contrast and a first-order Taylor expansion give
\[
\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}-\boldsymbol\tau)
=C_\tau(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0;\iota)
\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)+o_p(1),
\]
whose covariance is the declared \(V_\tau\).

The empirical same-well products consistently estimate every \(\Omega_j\) by the stratified lemma.  Continuity of all matrix products and inverses on the certified nonsingular neighborhood, together with consistency of \(\widehat\theta\), proves plug-in consistency for \(\Sigma_g,V_\theta,V_\tau\).  The contrast-nondegeneracy assumption makes every reported scalar limiting variance strictly positive.  Slutsky's theorem then gives pointwise coverage \(1-\alpha\) for each scalar Wald interval.  No uniform assertion at a graph or variance boundary is used.

Finally, the covariance factorization and spectral submultiplicativity give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Sigma_g\|_2
&=\|D_gA_{\mathcal T}D_h^{-1}\Sigma_h
D_h^{-1}A_{\mathcal T}^{\mathsf T}D_g\|_2\\
&\leq\|D_g\|_2^2\|A_{\mathcal T}\|_2^2
\|D_h^{-1}\|_2^2\|\Sigma_h\|_2\\
&=\|\operatorname{diag}(g)\|_2^2\|M^+\|_2^2
\|\operatorname{diag}(h)^{-1}\|_2^2\|\Sigma_h\|_2,
\end{aligned}
\]
because \(\|M^+\otimes I_L\|_2=\|M^+\|_2\).  This is the stated pooling-amplification bound.

The fixed matrix has determinant \(1\), so it is invertible and its Moore--Penrose inverse is its ordinary inverse:
\[
M_0^+=M_0^{-1}
=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The rank-frontier identity gives
\[
\begin{pmatrix}\log G_1\\ \log G_2\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}\log H_1\\ \log H_2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
All PGFs are strictly positive on \((0,1]^p\), so exponentiation and ordinary division are valid and yield
\[
G_1=\frac{H_1^2}{H_2},\qquad G_2=\frac{H_2}{H_1}.
\]

Let \(\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\) have equal moment vectors.  If
\(\|\theta-\theta'\|_2<r_{\mathrm{id}}\), validity of the recorded cover puts them in a common chart \(C_{\boldsymbol d c}\).  Equality of moment vectors implies equality after projection, and hence
\[
0=\langle\phi_{\boldsymbol d c}(\theta)
-\phi_{\boldsymbol d c}(\theta'),\theta-\theta'\rangle
\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}\|\theta-\theta'\|_2^2.
\]
Since \(\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}>0\), this forces \(\theta=\theta'\).  If instead their distance is at least \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\), the certified remote bound gives
\[
\|m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta)
-m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta')\|_W^2
\geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}>0,
\]
contradicting equality.  When the remote set is empty this second case cannot occur.  Thus the moment map is globally injective.

For \(g_0=m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta_0)\), positive definiteness of \(W\) gives
\[
Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta;g_0)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta)=g_0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\theta=\theta_0.
\]
The displayed remote bound supplies the asserted quantitative separation outside the local neighborhood.

theorem.statement: For every finite admissible design class, the certified Pareto frontier is exactly computable by finite enumeration, certified infeasibility pruning, and certified dominance pruning.  A candidate may be discarded without running its remaining certificate tasks whenever a proved upper envelope for all of its attainable objective coordinates is weakly dominated, with one strict coordinate, by the proved lower objective vector of an already certified candidate.  After all unpruned candidates terminate, pairwise comparison of their certified output vectors returns exactly \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\).  No assumption in the frozen core guarantees a strict reduction from exhaustive evaluation in the worst case: all admissible candidates can remain feasible and mutually nondominated.
theorem.proof_tex:
Finiteness follows directly from the caps.  There are finitely many integers \(J\), finitely many matrices
\[
M\in\{0,\ldots,m_{\max}\}^{J\times K},
\]
finitely many nonempty grid subsets of the finite set
\(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{cand}}\) of size at most \(L_{\max}\), finitely many allocations and well caps in the declared finite sets, and finitely many integer truncation, moment, Taylor, subdivision, and precision choices under \(\mathfrak b\).  The additional inequality
\(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\leq B_{\max}\) only removes candidates.  Thus
\(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}=\{\Xi_1,\ldots,\Xi_N\}\) for some finite \(N\).

For a certified candidate define the maximization-oriented vector
\[
y(\Xi)=\bigl(
\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T},
\underline\kappa_{\mathcal T},
\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T},
\underline\mu_{\mathcal T},
-N_{\mathrm{req}},-w_{\mathrm{cert}},-\mathfrak B(\Xi)
\bigr). \tag{34}
\]
Write \(y\succeq y'\) when every coordinate is at least the corresponding coordinate of \(y'\), and \(y\succ_{\!P}y'\) when additionally one inequality is strict.  The following finite algorithm is explicit.

First order candidates lexicographically by their finite encodings.  Apply the exact syntax, rank, simplex, box, and arithmetic-cap tests.  Maintain the set \(C\) of completed certified candidates.  For an unfinished candidate \(x\), interval computations may maintain an upper envelope \(U(x)\) satisfying \(y(x)\preceq U(x)\) for every possible certified completion.  If some \(c\in C\) satisfies \(y(c)\succ_{\!P}U(x)\), discard \(x\).  This is sound because transitivity would give \(y(c)\succ_{\!P}y(x)\).  Otherwise run the remaining finite certificate tasks.  At termination remove from \(C\) every \(x\) for which another \(c\in C\) has \(y(c)\succ_{\!P}y(x)\).

The certificate soundness theorem proves every infeasibility decision and every coordinate bound used by this algorithm.  A discarded candidate cannot be Pareto maximal by the preceding inequality.  Every retained candidate is certified and is not dominated by any certified candidate, because all unpruned candidates have terminated and the final comparison is exhaustive over \(C\).  Conversely every certified nondominated candidate is neither infeasible nor soundly dominated, so it survives.  The output is therefore exactly \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\).

The frozen assumptions impose no theorem forcing an untested candidate to be infeasible or dominated.  A literal witness to the absence of a uniform strict-subenumeration guarantee is any admissible instance whose candidate sets and caps leave a singleton \(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}=\{\Xi\}\) with \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)=\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\): its frontier is \(\{\Xi\}\), so its sole candidate must survive the tests that establish certification.  More generally, pairwise incomparable certified vectors cannot be dominance-pruned.  Thus the pruning characterization is exact and often useful, but a worst-case need to evaluate every surviving candidate cannot be removed without an additional monotonicity or dominance theorem.

Let \(F:X\to\mathbb R^d\) be continuously differentiable on a compact box \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\), let \(x\in X\), let \(C\) be nonsingular, and let \(\boldsymbol J_F(X)\) enclose every Jacobian on \(X\).  If
\[
x-CF(x)+\{I-C A:A\in\boldsymbol J_F(X)\}(X-x)
\subset\operatorname{int}(X),
\]
then \(F\) has a zero in \(X\).

added_lemmas.statement: On every fixed graph box in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), all count moments are finite uniformly over the box; the joint mass function, every component PGF on \((0,1)^p\), and every fixed truncated-factorization contrast are twice continuously differentiable in the coefficients, with differentiation permitted term by term.  For each fixed graph tuple, the coefficient-to-law map is injective and has injective differential at every coefficient vector.  The compact law images of two distinct graph tuples are disjoint.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a graph tuple \(\boldsymbol d\).  It is enough to argue one type at a time, because its joint mass is a factor in the type product and the parameter blocks of distinct types are disjoint.  Choose a topological ordering of the vertices.  At a root, every moment of \(V_s\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\alpha_s)\) is a polynomial in \(\alpha_s\), hence is bounded uniformly on the compact coefficient box.  Suppose the claim is known for all predecessors of a non-root \(s\).  Conditional on its parents,
\[
\mathbb E[V_s^m\mid V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)}]
=\sum_{k=0}^m
\left\{\begin{matrix}m\\k\end{matrix}\right\}
\lambda_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})^k .
\]
The rate is a polynomial in predecessor counts with coefficients bounded on the box.  Expanding its powers and applying Holder's inequality bounds every displayed expectation by finitely many predecessor moments.  Induction gives, for every integer \(m\geq0\),
\[
\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}}\mathbb E_\theta
\left(\sum_{s=1}^pV_s\right)^m<\infty. \tag{1}
\]
The same induction applies after fixing one intervention coordinate at either \(1\) or \(2\).

Every rate has a uniform positive lower bound.  If \(t\) indexes the intercept or one edge coefficient in the conditional rate of node \(s\), put
\[
a_{st}(v_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})
\in\{1,v_k^{q_{sk}}:k\in\operatorname{pa}(s)\}.
\]
For the positive joint mass \(p_\theta(v)\),
\[
\partial_t\log p_\theta(v)
=a_{st}(v_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})
\left\{\frac{v_s}{\lambda_s(v_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})}-1\right\}. \tag{2}
\]
First and second derivatives of \(p_\theta(v)\) are therefore \(p_\theta(v)\) times functions bounded uniformly by a fixed polynomial in \(v\).  Equation (1) supplies a summable uniform majorant, first on a slightly larger positive coefficient box and then on the given compact box.  Dominated convergence consequently permits two termwise derivatives of the mass, PGF, intervened mass, and the two contrast expectations.  It also gives their continuity.

The observational law identifies its positive conditional masses at every parent vector, hence identifies
\[
\lambda_s(x)=\mathbb E_\theta[V_s\mid
V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)}=x].
\]
Evaluating at \(x=0\) gives \(\alpha_s\), and evaluating at the parent vector having coordinate \(k\) equal to \(1\) and all other coordinates zero gives
\[
b_{sk}=\lambda_s(e_k)-\lambda_s(0).
\]
Thus the parameter-to-law map is injective within a fixed graph.

For differential injectivity, collect the node-\(s\) scores from (2) into
\[
S_s=f_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})
\frac{V_s-\lambda_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})}
{\lambda_s(V_{\operatorname{pa}(s)})},
\qquad
f_s=(1,(V_k^{q_{sk}})_{k\in\operatorname{pa}(s)})^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Along the topological filtration these are martingale differences.  Hence different node blocks are orthogonal, and the information block is
\[
I_s=\mathbb E_\theta\!\left[
\frac{f_sf_s^{\mathsf T}}{\lambda_s}\right]. \tag{3}
\]
If \(c^{\mathsf T}I_sc=0\), positivity of the joint mass implies \(c^{\mathsf T}f_s(x)=0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb N_0^{|\operatorname{pa}(s)|}\).  Evaluation at zero and then with one coordinate equal to \(1\) forces every coordinate of \(c\) to vanish.  Thus (3) is positive definite, and every nonzero parameter direction \(a\) has \(\mathbb E_\theta[(a^{\mathsf T}S)^2]>0\).

Suppose its directional PGF derivative vanished on a nonempty open box in \((0,1)^p\).  It is the absolutely convergent signed power series
\[
\sum_{v\in\mathbb N_0^p}p_\theta(v)
a^{\mathsf T}S(v)z^v. \tag{4}
\]
Successive one-variable power-series uniqueness shows every coefficient in (4) is zero.  For completeness, an absolutely convergent one-variable power series that is zero on an open subinterval has all Taylor derivatives zero at every interior point; its Taylor expansion therefore vanishes on the overlapping interval of convergence, and finitely many overlapping intervals continue the equality to every compact subinterval of \((0,1)\).  After continuation down to zero, division by the least nonzero power and passage to zero rules out a nonzero coefficient.  Fixing the other coordinates and iterating this argument over the \(p\) coordinates proves the multivariate assertion.  This contradicts the strictly positive variance just obtained.  The differential is therefore injective.

Finally, the proposition on polynomial-class inclusion and the cited CPCM DAG-identification lemma imply that two different labeled graph tuples cannot generate the same law.  Continuity proved above sends compact coefficient boxes to compact law images, so those distinct images are disjoint compact sets.  All assertions also hold after stacking the finitely many types.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under full column rank and the positive stable row allocation, for either sample split with total size \(N\),
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat h-h)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_h),
\qquad
\sqrt N(\widehat g-g)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_g),
\]
where \(\Sigma_h,\Sigma_g\) are those in \(\mathrm{def{:}replicate\text{-}pgf\text{-}covariance}\).  The same-well cross-grid entries are
\[
(\Omega_j)_{\ell\ell'}
=H_j(z_\ell\odot z_{\ell'})
-H_j(z_\ell)H_j(z_{\ell'}).
\]
Replacing the expectations, row fractions, and recovered moments by their empirical analogues gives a consistent plug-in covariance estimator.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For row \(j\), define the bounded vector
\[
U_{ji}=(z_\ell^{B_{ji}})_{\ell=1}^L,\qquad
\widehat h_j=\frac1{n_j}\sum_{i=1}^{n_j}U_{ji}.
\]
Its mean is \(h_j=(H_j(z_\ell))_\ell\).  Because
\[
z_\ell^{B_{ji}}z_{\ell'}^{B_{ji}}
=(z_\ell\odot z_{\ell'})^{B_{ji}},
\]
its covariance is exactly \(\Omega_j\) as displayed in the claim.  The bounded-vector central limit theorem gives
\[
\sqrt{n_j}(\widehat h_j-h_j)\Rightarrow
\mathcal N(0,\Omega_j).
\]
The row samples are independent, and \(n_j/N\to\rho_j>0\).  Stacking the finitely many rows and multiplying row \(j\) by
\(\sqrt{N/n_j}\) therefore gives
\[
\sqrt N(\widehat h-h)\Rightarrow
\mathcal N\!\left(0,
\operatorname{blockdiag}(\Omega_j/\rho_j)_{j=1}^J\right)
=\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_h). \tag{5}
\]

Every coordinate of \(h\) is strictly positive because every integrand \(z_\ell^{B_{ji}}\) is strictly positive.  On the positive orthant define
\[
F(x)=\exp\{A_{\mathcal T}\log x\},
\qquad A_{\mathcal T}=M^+\otimes I_L.
\]
Full column rank and the rank-frontier identity give \(F(h)=g\), while
\[
DF(h)=D_gA_{\mathcal T}D_h^{-1}. \tag{6}
\]
Applying the differentiable-map part of the cited finite-vector limit result to (5) and (6) yields
\[
\Sigma_g
=D_gA_{\mathcal T}D_h^{-1}\Sigma_h
D_h^{-1}A_{\mathcal T}^{\mathsf T}D_g,
\]
which is the declared covariance.

For consistency, every coordinate of the empirical first and second products is an average of bounded variables.  Its variance is \(O(n_j^{-1})\), so Chebyshev's inequality gives convergence in probability.  Since \(n_j/N\to\rho_j>0\), empirical row fractions converge as well.  Matrix multiplication, coordinatewise logarithm on the positive orthant, and the diagonal maps are continuous; hence substitution in (5)--(6) consistently estimates both covariance matrices.

It rejects \(\rho\notin\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) before covariance or required-well evaluation. proposed.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\), fix \(\iota\), and let \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)=\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\). Suppose the true pooled model has \(\boldsymbol D_0\in\mathfrak G\) and \(\theta_0\in\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol D_0}\), the normalized allocation obeys \(\rho\in\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) with \(\rho_j>0\) for every row and \(n_{Sj}/N_S\to\rho_j\) for \(S\in\{A,B\}\), and the weighting and nondegeneracy conditions hold.
